meta.title: Candidate signal register
meta.note: Hypotheses with named falsifiers. None has been tested; no result is claimed.

signals.hypothesis: Opponent-adjusted, sequentially-updated efficiency predicts spread/total outcomes better than raw yards.
signals.falsifier: No out-of-sample log-loss improvement over a neutral baseline.

signals.hypothesis: Officially listed starters being ruled Out moves the fair line by more than the market adjusts, net of margin.
signals.falsifier: Effect disappears once the closing quote is used, or fails leave-one-team-out.
signals.status: partially computable - description side held, price side blocked

signals.hypothesis: Clubs already running high snap-share concentration on non-starters degrade faster when another starter is lost.
signals.falsifier: Snap-share concentration adds no predictive power conditional on availability.

signals.hypothesis: Short-week and cross-country travel have a small but persistent effect on totals and second-half scoring.
signals.falsifier: Effect vanishes under venue fixed effects.

signals.hypothesis: Penalty rate and total-spot discipline persist per crew year over year.
Sustained wind suppresses totals more than precipitation does.
signals.falsifier: No conditional effect after controlling for team tendencies.

signals.hypothesis: Price movement encodes information about availability before it is official.
signals.falsifier: n/a - benchmark discipline: this is a comparison series, never a model input.
